title: Text-to-SQL Interface with Guardrails and Hallucination Detection
summary: An approval-gated analyst console that turns bounded natural-language questions into policy-checked, read-only SQL over disclosed synthetic data.
outcome: Reviewers can inspect SQL, assumptions, schema lineage, policy checks, and a bounded result preview before one single-use execution; unsafe, malformed, identifier-exposing, and hallucinated-schema queries fail closed.

story.recruiterSummary: Natural-language analytics is attractive because it lowers the barrier to data access, but executing model-generated SQL directly creates obvious security, privacy, and correctness risk. This project turns that risky shortcut into a reviewable workflow: the model may propose, a deterministic policy engine must validate, and a person must approve one bounded read-only preview.
story.technicalNarrative: FastAPI separates proposal from execution. Azure OpenAI receives only an identifier-excluding semantic catalog through Microsoft Entra authentication; SQLGlot checks statement shape, functions, tables, columns, identifier projection, and ranking semantics; DuckDB EXPLAIN and resource limits run before a short-lived approval can be consumed. Execution revalidates both SQL policy and the active snapshot checksum.
scalabilityRoadmap: Replace ephemeral SQLite with an owner-approved transactional store and prove cross-replica single-use consumption
Enable single-tenant Microsoft Entra authentication and verify unauthenticated denial
Replace process-local rate and proposal budgets with durable distributed controls before multi-replica hosting
Add alerting, budget ownership, availability/error monitoring, and an owner-approved load envelope
Expand semantic evaluation with reviewer-approved equivalent SQL rather than literal query matching
story.executiveSummary: A guarded Text-to-SQL first demo that makes model output inspectable, evidence-linked, and explicitly non-production.
story.intendedUser: A data analyst or technical reviewer evaluating governed natural-language access to a classified synthetic payments model.

example.title: Generate, review, and approve one bounded query
steps: Choose or enter an analytical question over the disclosed semantic catalog
Inspect proposed SQL, assumptions, referenced fields, policy checks, and EXPLAIN summary
Approve one short-lived token-bound execution or let the system refuse the request
Review a maximum 100-row preview that excludes identifier-like fields

technologyDecisions.technology: Azure OpenAI with Microsoft Entra ID
technologyDecisions.rationale: Keeps provider credentials out of the repository and supports managed identity in Azure.
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: Identity and role configuration add operational setup but remove long-lived application secrets.

technologyDecisions.rationale: Provides parser-backed structural policy and database-level validation before execution.
technologyDecisions.alternative: Regex filtering or direct model execution
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: The policy intentionally rejects ambiguous or unsupported SQL and still requires semantic human review.

technologyDecisions.rationale: Provides five-minute single-use approval persistence for a one-replica temporary demo.
technologyDecisions.tradeoff: Simple and low-cost, but restart-sensitive and unsuitable for protected multi-replica hosting.

limitations: The current endpoint is anonymous and has no caller authorization.
The deployed rate and proposal-budget controls are process-local and reset after scale-to-zero or restart.
Approval state is ephemeral and single-replica.
The model can still propose semantically wrong SQL, so human review remains mandatory.
The demo expiry requires owner teardown; the application cannot delete its own Azure resources.

bulletCandidates.bullet: Built an approval-gated Text-to-SQL service with Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Entra ID, SQLGlot, FastAPI, and read-only DuckDB execution, matching expected outcomes across 18 deterministic safety and correctness cases.

Designed a checksum-pinned synthetic-data release boundary that removes source account identifiers, blocks raw and approved snapshots from the container image, and exposes only classified fields to model context and previews.

Delivered and verified a scale-to-zero Azure Container Apps demo with immutable revision, image-digest, fixture-boundary, and deployed-control evidence while explicitly separating anonymous exposure from production readiness.
